name: calcite
reference: Ghosh 1999, Opt. Commun. 163, 95-102; Bloss 1961/Hartshorne & Stuart classic mineralogy references for walk-off convention
notes: negative uniaxial (n_e<n_o at all visible wavelengths: n_o(590nm)=1.658 > n_e(590nm)=1.486, delta_n=-0.172); walk-off angle rho=atan[(n_o/n_e)^2 * tan(theta)] - theta, max walk-off ~6.2 deg occurs near internal angle theta~45 deg from optic axis at 590nm; classic Nicol/Glan-Thompson prism and beam-displacer material

name: quartz
notes: positive uniaxial (n_e>n_o at all visible wavelengths: n_o(589nm)=1.5443 < n_e(589nm)=1.5534, delta_n=+0.0091); birefringence ~19x weaker than calcite so walk-off is correspondingly small (walk-off ~0.34 deg at theta=45 deg internal angle at 589nm, computed from rho=atan[(n_o/n_e)^2*tan(theta)]-theta); standard waveplate/retarder material (quartz order-sorting filters, Babinet-Soleil compensators)

name: sapphire
reference: Malitson & Dodge 1972 (Al2O3 o-ray and e-ray Sellmeier), as tabulated by refractiveindex.info
notes: negative uniaxial (n_e<n_o: n_o(589nm)=1.7682 > n_e(589nm)=1.7600, delta_n=-0.0082); weak birefringence similar in magnitude to quartz, so walk-off is small (walk-off ~0.27 deg at theta=45 deg internal angle at 589nm, computed from rho=atan[(n_o/n_e)^2*tan(theta)]-theta using n_o=1.7682,n_e=1.7600); used for durable c-axis windows/waveplates where quartz is too soft or not thermally/chemically robust enough
